scope_rule: All listed capability families remain required. A passing subset is not full-browser qualification.

capabilities.description: HTML parsing, DOM, events, custom elements, and shadow DOM
CSS syntax, cascade, selectors, layout families, fragmentation, and animation
Unicode, OpenType, multilingual shaping, fallback, selection, and rasterization
ECMAScript semantics, builtins, RegExp, BigInt, modules, GC, and Intl
Web IDL conversions, platform objects, and exception behavior
URL, encoding, Fetch, redirects, cookies, HTTP behavior, and secure transport integration
Storage, IndexedDB, workers, service workers, streams, and offline applications
SVG, canvas, image formats, animation, and decoder limits
Audio, video, media synchronization, capture, and platform policy
Guest WebGL and WebGPU, separate from internal GPU acceleration
Origins, secure contexts, CSP, permissions, broker policy, and containment
Clipboard, files, notifications, cryptography, WebAuthn, WebSockets, WebRTC, and related declared app APIs
Keyboard, pointer, touch, IME, focus, accessibility, zoom, and printing
Address bar, page, navigation, history, downloads, app windows, profiles, restore, and diagnostics, delivered by a Rust shell with engine-rendered chrome that uses only the public embedding contract
C ABI, Zig API, process protocol, Wasm embedding, the first-party Rust wrapper that carries the browser shell, and qualified language wrappers
Native Windows, Linux, macOS, architecture variants, and separately declared mobile targets
Named workload budgets for startup, tail latency, memory, binary size, and qualified power measurements
Releases, provenance, license, security response, maintainer continuity, and downstream integration

known_policy_questions: DRM platform access and resulting compatibility claims
completion_policy: Mechanical qualification does not prove the absence of every bug. New standards and defects remain maintenance work.
